claims.claim: Cursor says worktrees give each task isolated files, dependencies, and changes while the main checkout stays untouched.
claims.exact_excerpt: Worktrees let Agent work in isolated Git checkouts. Each task gets its own files, dependencies, and changes while your main checkout stays untouched.

claims.claim: Cursor says each best-of-N run gets its own worktree and remains isolated from other candidates and the main checkout.
claims.exact_excerpt: Each run gets its own worktree, so the candidates stay isolated from each other and from your main checkout.

claims.claim: Git linked worktrees share repository state but keep HEAD, index, and other per-worktree files separate.
claims.exact_excerpt: The new worktree is linked to the current repository, sharing everything except per-worktree files such as `HEAD`, `index`, etc.

claims.claim: Git refuses, absent force, to create a worktree for a branch already checked out elsewhere.
claims.exact_excerpt: By default, `add` refuses to create a new worktree when _<commit-ish>_ is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree

claims.claim: Ordinary refs under refs/ are shared across worktrees even though HEAD is per-worktree.
claims.exact_excerpt: In general, all pseudo refs are per-worktree and all refs starting with `refs/` are shared.
